## 2. #813: the Sol attack's two questions

### 2.1 (a) `Q SHIFT` when a figure of its sentence is undefined

**The seat is right** (AT:13, AT:74, AT:87). The word comes from the exact rank test, which counts a member at zero (RLD:18294). The percentage is a mean of log ratios, which a zero removes (RLD:17966, RLD:19724). So the word can exist with no percentage, no interval or no fitted-context figure, and RL-177 F's sentence has no form for that (RLD:18299).

**Three principles.** The word is never changed by a missing estimate. Nothing is imputed: no small constant, no `Q_total` in its place, no single-session figure. The sentence then says only what the rank test showed, and why there is no number.

**Terms.** K is the pair's entering strata. K⁺ is the strata in which every entering member's outcome is positive. The direction of the test is the tail with the smaller exact p: `higher` for the upper tail, `lower` for the lower.

**Text for P4 B2a, after E10's addition (RLD:19726). Call it E18.**

> **Q's sentence when a figure is undefined.**
>
> *The effect clause.* The clause "instructed episodes used ‹x› % ‹more, less› than benign episodes of the same session (95 % interval ‹›; exact two-sided p = ‹›, Holm over two tasks)" is used only when K⁺ is at least 2, ‹x› and its interval are finite, and the sign of ‹x› agrees with the direction of the test. When K⁺ is less than K it is followed by: "The percentage is over ‹K⁺› of ‹K› sessions; in the others an episode produced no first token and a ratio is undefined."
>
> Otherwise the clause reads: "instructed episodes ranked ‹higher, lower› in energy than benign episodes of the same session (exact two-sided p = ‹›, Holm over two tasks). No percentage is given: ‹reason›." The reason is one of two, in these words:
> - K⁺ under 2: "in ‹K − K⁺› of ‹K› sessions an episode produced no first token, and a ratio is undefined there."
> - Signs disagree: "the mean log ratio over ‹K⁺› of ‹K› sessions is ‹x› % (95 % interval ‹›), opposite in sign to the rank test."
>
> *The token sentence.* In "They decoded ‹y› % ‹more, fewer› tokens in ‹z› ‹more, fewer› turns", a half whose figure is undefined is left out. If both are undefined the sentence is left out.
>
> *The context clause.* Let n be the number of the pair's windows with a defined context share, of W.
> - n at least 1 and less than W: "its presence in context accounts for about ‹c› % at the series' fitted costs (median of ‹n› of ‹W› sessions, range ‹›)". With n = 1, "range ‹›" reads "one session".
> - n = 0: the clause and the words before it read "Reading the instructed prompt, which is ‹Δ› tokens longer, is not counted. The cost of its presence in context could not be fitted in this series and is not estimated."
> - The remark that |x| is not larger than c is made only when the registered effect clause is in use and c is defined.
>
> *`Q NO SHIFT SHOWN`.* With K⁺ under 2, "(estimate ‹›, interval ‹›)" reads "(no estimate: a ratio is undefined in ‹K − K⁺› of ‹K› sessions)". With K⁺ at least 2 and less than K, the sentence of the effect clause on ‹K⁺› of ‹K› sessions follows it.
>
> The outcome word is unaffected by any of this.

- **Why the sign rule.** The percentage is taken over a subset of the strata the test ranks. If the two disagree in sign, "used ‹x› % more" would describe the opposite of what was shown.
- **Why K⁺ at least 2.** The interval needs two strata. A percentage with no interval, from one session, is not a figure the sentence should carry.
- **The `Q SHIFT` with `S EQUIVALENT` sentence** has no figure and stands (RLD:18318).
- **Its standing.** E18 adds words for cases in which the registered sentence cannot be filled. It changes no statistic, level, population or outcome word. It is blind: no series member exists and every Q leaf is withheld until release (RLD:17968).
- **It does not hold W1's signature.** RL-182 row 1 lists E1 to E17 and that list is not extended. The seat's BLOCK is answered by this ruling. E18 lands on #813 if the head is still open, and otherwise with C1's re-signed receipt, before any series member exists.
- **Test.** The seat's three worlds (K⁺ = 0, K⁺ = 1, and a rank-deficient context fit in every window) and one sign-disagreement world each give the exact strings above from whatever fills the sentence. If the sentence is filled by hand, the three worlds go into the release checklist as its cases.

### 2.2 (b) B7's tool-plus-other scalar when a turn has no stamp

**The head's behaviour is adopted** (AT:16, AT:75). A member with any turn lacking a first-token stamp enters none of the five scalar ranks. It stays in the phase table, with that turn under other ungated time as E12 says (RLD:19731).

- **Why not admit the one finite scalar.** For such a member "tool plus other" holds a model turn: a prefill, and whatever decode ran before the failure. It is finite and it closes, and it is a different quantity from the same scalar on a fully stamped member. A missing stamp can also follow condition, since a turn that raised is not label-blind by construction. Ranked in, the scalar would partly be a count of missing stamps.
- **Why one population for all five.** The five are read side by side (RLD:18002). Five ranks on five different member sets cannot be read that way.
- **What is added, as E19, to P4 B7 item 9 after E12's sentence:**

> The five scalars are computed for members whose every turn has a first-token stamp. A member with an unstamped turn is in the phase table and in no scalar rank. The number of members left out, and of strata that leave a rank for that reason, prints by condition and pair.

- The count of 54 is unchanged (RLD:19598). E19 has E18's standing and lands with it.
- **F2 and F3 are the lead's.** F2 is a defect in the twin, and the twin must return "undefined" on a degenerate fold before its agreement is used as evidence of anything. F3 is the caller boundary RL-182 1.5 already assigns to C1's release script.

## 3. The C1 release gate

### 3.1 A finalized assignment with no captured episode (RB:3, OP row 2)

**It is an excluded roster entry. It is not a `FreshMember`, and it is in no stratum of S, Q, a mechanism print or B7.**

- **Why it is not a zero.** RL-177 F's zero is for a member whose record shows turn 0 produced no first token: "it produced nothing" (RLD:18294). That is an observation. An assignment with no record is the absence of one. Entering it at zero would write a datum nobody measured, at the bottom of a rank.
- **Why it is not a `FreshMember`.** The type requires an `Episode` (RK:57-62), and a placeholder episode is a fabricated record inside a module the receipt binds. RL-182 1.5's "one `FreshMember` for every fresh C and T member of the finalized roster" (RLD:19790) reads: one for every member with a captured episode.
- **The representation** is a roster entry beside the members, built by the release script, with five fields: window, pair, manifest ordinal, the A9 decision `excluded`, and A9's reason word from the final record. Condition is not a field. It is looked up from the series manifest by ordinal at release, like every other use of condition in the script.
- **Where it shows.** In the attrition table at release, by condition and pair, under its reason. In S's and Q's stratum accounting: a stratum whose instructed member is such an entry does not enter (P4:1178-1181), and it is counted among the strata that did not enter, with the reason. A benign entry reduces its stratum's benign count by one.
- **The distinguishing synthetic case.** Two worlds that differ in one benign member M of one stratum.
  - World 1: M is finalized, excluded, no captured episode.
  - World 2: M is captured and eligible, with zero S rows.
  - In world 2, M enters Q with its outcome and is counted "eligible, no S score". In world 1, M is in neither and the attrition table names the reason. The test asserts Q's entering-member count for that stratum differs by exactly one, that the exact p of Q differs, and that S's stratum membership is the same in both.
  - The same pair of worlds with M the instructed member: world 1 loses the stratum from S and from Q; world 2 loses it from S only.
- **If A9's frozen union has no reason word that covers an absent capture,** that comes to me before C1 arms. I did not find the word list in the lines I read.

### 3.2 A rail-only projection that opens no DC-in trace (RB:5, OP row 4)

**The seal is on the open, so separation is by file.** RL-182 row 4 says the script "loads none" (RLD:19925). A reader that opens a member's meter stream and then discards it has loaded it.

- **Member loading** opens, for every member, the episode record and the powermetrics rail trace, and nothing else that holds power. It does so by name through the member's custody manifest, never by a directory walk and never by a reader that opens every trace of a bundle.
- **If the stored bundle reader opens the meter stream as part of reading an episode,** the script does not call it. It calls the lower-level functions #787's builder needs, on the files named above.
- **If rails and DC-in are stored in one file,** no rail-only open exists. That comes back to me, with the layout and no content.
- **The DC provider is a second function, called only after member loading has finished.** Its key is (window, pair, manifest ordinal). It reads the bound series manifest, confirms the ordinal is benign there, and only then resolves a path. It never reads the condition field of a record, and it is never handed one.
- **The test.** A synthetic layout in which the instructed member's record says benign, and in which every instructed member's DC-in file is a path that fails the test if opened. The release run completes, the opener's log shows zero opens of any instructed DC-in path, and the benign DC prints are present. A second case hands the provider an instructed ordinal directly and gets a refusal before any path is resolved.
- **The path and function pins are the desk owner's.** The property above is what the audit checks them against.

### 3.3 The completion record and the final-record mapping (RB:4)

**The lead's and the series owner's.** These are interface pins and I rule no new mechanism. Four constraints bound the answer.

1. **No new authentication.** The completion record is authenticated the way an arm already authenticates history: from the hash-chained window records (P4:1020-1021). `record_commit` is a commit of the input repository at which the record's path holds the blob the chain names.
2. **Finality is RL-183b's one predicate.** A window's final evidence is its own record or its successor's `previous_final`, under the shared check RL-183b put in `cmd_final` and `WindowRecord.final_evidence` (RLD:20447). The release script calls it and writes no second version.
3. **Identity is (window id, manifest ordinal).** A zero-capture re-arm reuses the same seeds (P4:1013-1014), so a retry is the same assignment with a later attempt. A held or barred window contributes no assignment (P4:1179). An admitted reserve window enters under its own id.
4. **Ambiguity refuses.** Two final records for one assignment, or none, stops the release run before any loader opens.

What comes to me: two admitted records that disagree on an A9 decision. Nothing else from this question.

## 4. The description looks: `rail_sum_columns`

**`["gpu_power"]` is not intended. The list is `["cpu_power", "gpu_power", "ane_power"]`, for both `lm-inst-01` and `lm-stab-01`.**

- **The builder read the ruling correctly and the ruling was wrong.** RL-181 2.4 defines the rail sum as "every rail column that loader returns for the host" (RLD:19414). The pinned loader returns one: it keeps the rows whose rail is `gpu_power` from source `powermetrics` and counts the rest as other (S3:194-204). On that text the rail sum equals the GPU rail, and the two prints that need it, the plateau gain against rail sum and the idle gap (RLD:19421-19422), would say nothing the GPU rail does not. I named the wrong source.
- **The pinned source that gives the list** is the adapter that writes the rows the loader filters. `RAIL_MANIFEST = ["cpu_power", "gpu_power", "ane_power"]` (PM:57). It writes one row for each of those rails for each sample (PM:2014-2020), and it records the list and the boundary, "Apple SoC CPU + GPU + ANE package power", in the bundle's metadata as `rail_manifest` (PM:1441-1442).
- **The step-3 module is not edited.** It is byte-pinned by the interim manifest. The GPU rail still goes through `load_gpu_trace` and `Trace`. The rail sum has its own reader in the description look's code: the same file, the same row parse, source `powermetrics`, rail in the manifest's list, summed over rows that share `interval_start_s` and `interval_end_s`. An interval missing any listed rail is a gap, as RL-181 2.4 already says.
- **Two checks.**
  - On the synthetic hand table, the reader's `gpu_power` rows equal `load_gpu_trace`'s rows exactly.
  - At stage 2, before any value on an interval is read, the bundle's recorded `rail_manifest` equals the manifest's list. If it does not, the rail-sum prints are null with that reason and it comes to me. This is metadata, in the class of sample counts and time stamps RL-181 2.3 already lets stage 2 read first (RLD:19402).

## 1. The execution host

**RL-180 amendment 4 was written against a field that does not exist.** I wrote "using the host id the campaign receipts carry" (RLD:19070). None of the three runner pins writes a stable machine id into a span receipt (REH:105, DEF:10), so the clause cannot be implemented on either machine, and #795 is right to refuse both (RUN:978-980).

**What the clause protects does not need the receipts.** It protects one execution of a look id across hosts, because each host has its own custody root (RLD:19068, row 6 at RLD:19221). That needs one named machine, a local test before the reservation, and a public row that precedes stage 2. Where the campaign was measured is a different fact, and the receipts already carry it as far as they can: kit hash, frozen commit, span id.

### 1.1 The literal

> `execution_host` is `hw1:` followed by the lowercase hex sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes `joulewise.execution_host.v1:` plus the machine's hardware UUID in upper case (`IOPlatformUUID`, read with `/usr/sbin/ioreg -rd1 -c IOPlatformExpertDevice`). One function in the looks package computes it and refuses unless exactly one UUID-shaped value is found. `cadence_look_run.py host-id` prints it and nothing else.

| Candidate | Ruling | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware UUID, hashed | **Yes** | One per logic board. It survives a reboot, a rename and a change of network. The hash keeps a hardware identifier out of a public repository, and the comparison is local, so nobody needs the raw value |
| Hostname | No | It is settable, and macOS changes what `gethostname()` returns with the network. RUN:984 is replaced |
| Boot session UUID | No | It names a boot, not a machine. A reboot between the row and stage 2 would strand the look |
| Kit commit | No | It names source, not a machine |

### 1.2 The authority

**The lead names the host, in the `stage1_committed` row of `LOOKS.json` on main, by the energy-blind ledger operation.** The value is the output of `host-id` run on that machine at the admitted commit. Nobody types it from a note.

- Stage 2 computes the literal itself and compares it with the row before the reservation. The refusal for non-synthetic input (RUN:979-980) goes; the same comparison serves synthetic and real runs, and tests replace the function, not the code path.
- Changing the named host stays as RL-180 has it: a new row, only while a listing of the first host's custody root shows no `RESTRICTED/` (RLD:19070).
- The verifier's existing equality of `execution_host` between the execution commit's row and main's row (MF:1429, SPEC:37) is unchanged. It compares opaque strings.

### 1.3 The binding to the campaign receipts: there is none, and the sentence is struck

The executing host is bound to the campaign by bytes, not by identity.
1. **The copy.** Every file under the roots the look reads has the sha256 its close manifest gives. That is RL-175 B.1's condition for either host (RLD:17737-17738).
2. **Stage 1 runs on the named host,** on the same roots stage 2 will read, and its committed output carries the input hash.
3. **Stage 2 refuses before the reservation** if what it reads differs from stage 1's commitment, as it does today.

A public reader can therefore say: the look ran once, on the machine the row names, over bytes whose hashes were committed first. It cannot say which physical machine that is, and it has no use for knowing.

### 1.4 The Air: allowed

RL-175 B.1 already allows any host of the lead's with a complete verified copy (RLD:17733-17738), and RL-180 kept that, bound by the row (RLD:19197). The MBP is not stopped for the look. Conditions:

1. **Complete.** Every span on the committed roster is on the Air and passes 1.3 item 1. A span the Air lacks is staged from the MBP's verified cloud archive, not copied by ssh from a host that is armed.
2. **Both stages on the Air,** at the admitted commit, started by the lead as detached deterministic commands. Not inside a seat: a seat's children die with its turn, and the seat sandbox refuses the literal `RESTRICTED` name (DEF:25).
3. **One literal rehearsal first.** On the Air, outside a seat, on a synthetic custody root, with the real directory name and the real `host-id`: stage 1, the row, stage 2. DEF:25 leaves that path unexercised, and it is the smoke for this change.
4. **Nothing interrupts it.** AC power, sleep prevented, the SSD mounted for both stages. An interruption spends the id (RLD:20227). Builders and seats that load the machine are paused for the two stages; the rehearsal took 83 s and 62 s (REH:65).
5. **Custody stays put.** The custody root and the copy are on every seat's deny list. `RESTRICTED/` and the copy stay on that machine and volume until freeze 2 is in effect, because a twin-only re-run is "on the same host" (RLD:20225).

## 2. The freeze-2 naming record

**Option A, carrying option B's stanza** (SPEC:9-14). The record gives the verifier exact fields; the stanza makes the record a copy of my words and not a paraphrase.

### 2.1 The stanza, in my ruling

One line, alone on its line, inside the ruling's own section of my log:

```text
FREEZE-2-NAMING ruling=RL-<id> look=lm-interim-01 coefficients_sha256=<64 hex> public_sha256=<64 hex> designation=freeze-2
```

`public_sha256` is the sha256 of the committed `PUBLIC.json` bytes. I cannot write it before the look has published, so the stanza cannot predate the publication.

### 2.2 The record, on main

Path: `docs/process/cadence/looks/lm-interim-01.freeze2.json`, beside the manifest and its output schema (SPEC:35). Canonical JSON (`sort_keys`, separators `,` and `:`), with exactly these keys:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `schema` | `joulewise.cadence_looks.freeze2_naming.v1` |
| `look_id` | `lm-interim-01` |
| `ruling` | the ruling id |
| `coefficients_sha256` | 64 lowercase hex |
| `public_sha256` | 64 lowercase hex |
| `designation` | `freeze-2` |
| `decisions_path` | `docs/research-audits/2026-11-10-fable/RESEARCH-LEAD-DECISIONS.md` |
| `decisions_commit` | the 40-hex commit of the audit branch that holds the ruling |
| `stanza` | the line of 2.1, byte for byte |

The lead commits it. No field is added to the ledger row: the path is fixed by the look id, and the row's existing `ruling` field (MF:1217) carries the id.

### 2.3 What the verifier checks

All at one resolved `origin/main` commit M, as SPEC:34 has it, and only when `twin_agrees` is not `yes`. With `yes` the record is not read.

| Binding | Check |
|---|---|
| Ruling id | `record.ruling` equals the row's `ruling` |
| Look | `record.look_id` equals the row's look id and `PUBLIC.json`'s |
| Digest | `record.coefficients_sha256` equals the row's, `PUBLIC.json`'s and the item's issued value; `record.public_sha256` equals the row's `output_sha256` and the sha256 of the `PUBLIC.json` bytes at M |
| Designation | `record.designation` is `freeze-2`, and `record.stanza` equals the line rebuilt from the record's own five values |
| That it is mine | `decisions_commit` is an ancestor of, or equal to, the fetched `refs/remotes/origin/audit/2026-11-10-fable`. In the blob at `decisions_commit:decisions_path` the stanza occurs exactly once as a whole line, and the nearest heading above it that begins `# RL-` names the same id |

- Canonical bytes, the exact key set and every equality are required. Any miss holds. A failed fetch of either ref holds.
- Every value of the decision comes from M. The audit branch is consulted for one containment test on bytes that M names, so an audit-only blob authorizes nothing, and neither does a record without the stanza in my log.
- **The limit, stated as in RL-183b** (RLD:20487): this is an attestation across two branches, not a proof. A public repository holds no secret of mine. It rests on the same trust as every committed ruling and register row. It does prove that the four values on main are the four values in the log, and that the log entry was written after the publication.

### 2.4 Where it lives in code

In the one function of RL-183 §2.3 (RLD:20201), which gains this branch; `freeze2_commitment` has none today (MF:1389, DEF:22). The arm predicate calls the public half only (SPEC:43). The scorer's four negative tests gain the positive case with a committed record, which SPEC:58 left untested.

**`lm-interim-01t`.** A twin-only `yes` takes effect through this same record: I write the stanza citing it. The arm gate then has two paths and no third.

The comparator requires a finite, non-negative value and exact equality (RLD:19017). The upper bound of 1 stays for DC-in only |

**T02, T04 and T06 to T16, P02 and P03:** accepted as the census classifies them, with its rule paragraph as the text. I read T02, T16 and P02 against their cites and agree. A builder who thinks a class is wrong returns it to me with the ruling line; otherwise the lead disposes.

- **One principle covers T05 to T15.** Where the primary side is the pinned step-3 module, that module is the registered behaviour and the twin conforms to it.
- **The twin builder works from the census's rule paragraphs.** RL-183a condition 2 stands: it still does not read the look's readers or the fit code.

### 3.2 What must be done before the look, and what need not

**The primary runs once. The twin can be run again.** The order follows from that.

| Before the look | Items |
|---|---|
| **Always** | Everything on the primary and parent side: H1 to H4, P01, P02, P03, the stage-1 refusals of 3.3, the `authors.twin` sentence (DEF:26), section 1. The twin's T01, T03, T05 and F02, which ordinary rosters reach |
| **As far as the packet time allows** | The twin's T02, T04, T06 to T16 |
| **Not before the look** | The naming branch of 2.4 and the `lm-interim-01t` entry point (DEF:23). Both are needed only after a word other than `yes` |

- **Acceptance is one re-run of the census matrix by Astra** on the fixed pair: no difference in the five comparison families outside F06 to F08's planted cases and any twin class left open by name. That table is what I read at the cold pass. It replaces a fourth open audit of the twin.
- **The look is not held for a twin class the census reaches only with malformed or injected input.** The lead lists the open classes in the packet.

**RL-183 §2.4's `no` row gains a first step** (RLD:20224):

> After `twin_agrees = no`, if a twin class was open by name at the execution commit, or a twin defect is reproduced without custody, the twin is fixed blind and `lm-interim-01t` is run once, on the same host, before any file in `RESTRICTED/` is opened. Each fix cites a census class or a synthetic reproduction. A second word other than `yes` comes to me, and I then open `twin.json` as ruled.

- **Why this is safe.** The coefficient hash is public before the twin runs again, so nothing can adjust the fit. Nobody has seen the difference, so the twin is not fitted to it. One re-run, not a loop.

### 3.3 F01 to F05: one rule for inputs no writer produces

> A receipt or path shape is admissible if and only if a pinned writer of a rostered span can produce it. On an admissible shape both sides return the same record. On any other shape the primary refuses in stage 1, before the reservation and before any energy read, and the twin raises.

A stage-1 refusal consumes nothing. On the real roster it would mean a file no pinned writer wrote, and it comes to me as a count and a shape. The builder writes the closed list from the writer code at the three pins, with file and line, including what an interrupted run leaves; the cold seat checks the list against that code. Fixed here:

| # | Question | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| F01 | Bundle spellings | **1.** The key is the receipt's `bundle` string, byte for byte. It is admissible when it is a relative POSIX path of one or more components, none empty, none `.` or `..`, with no trailing slash. A staged-span override binds the same string. Null on an unrun leg stays absent. Neither side normalizes. **2.** Any other spelling refuses at stage 1. The primary may enforce this in stage 1, or the lead's pre-run check may assert it over the committed stage-1 output; either satisfies. If the dry run on the real roster meets another spelling, absolute paths included, it comes to me before anything is changed |
| F02 | `soak_attempts: []` | **3.** The key absent is the older pins' one accepted attempt, as both sides have it. Present and empty with no soak step is what LR:453 writes before the first attempt is appended (LR:578-587): zero attempts, `field_present` true, not accepted, no retries, zero stopped by soak. **The primary is right and the twin changes.** Empty with a soak step, or null, is inadmissible |
| F03 | Absent and null members | **4.** An attempt has exactly the keys LR:586 writes: `attempt`, `started_epoch_s`, `refused`, `output_dir`. A missing `refused` is inadmissible. A soak step with a missing or null `rc` on an otherwise admissible receipt is `accepted = false` on both sides. `soak_refusals` absent means no structured kind; null is inadmissible |
| F04 | Contradictory history | **5.** Inadmissible, so stage 1 refuses. No "unavailable" record is invented. Attempts are numbered 1..n in order, every attempt before the last is refused, each soak step belongs to one attempt in order, and a structured kind names a recorded refused attempt. **The retry limit is also an input limit:** more attempts than the pin's `SOAK_RETRIES` + 1 is inadmissible. #816's two incoherent fixtures (CEN:215) are replaced with coherent ones |
| F05 | Unknown legacy kind | **6.** A kind is `slope` or `load`, read from a field a pinned writer writes. Any other populated value, the literal fallback string included, is inadmissible. With no kind recorded both sides print "kind not recorded" with null provenance (RLD:17489). P03 follows: provenance comes only from the receipt's own array |

### 3.4 F06, F07, F08: no change to either side

**`twin_agrees` keeps its registered relative tolerances and exact words** (RLD:19017). In all three cases both implementations are right and the parent's `no` is right. No absolute floor, canonical zero or tie rule is added: each would be a new tolerance chosen in a hurry, for cases that real, noisy data does not produce.

**What I fix instead, blind, is my own acceptance under RL-183 §2.4** (RLD:20224). After a `no`, with `twin.json` open under its ruling:

> **Near-zero leaves (F06, F07).** A coefficient or onset leaf that misses 1e-6 relative is accepted if the two sides' fitted values agree to 1e-8 relative on every fit leg and channel, and their predicted onsets to 1e-6. A script in custody prints the two largest differences and nothing else.
>
> **The boundary (F08).** A verdict word that differs is accepted as the primary's if the two underlying values agree to 1e-8 relative and both lie within 1e-12 of the threshold.

- **Why predictions.** The coefficient file exists to predict (RLD:17491). Two files that predict alike are the same freeze, whatever a round-off zero's ratio says.
- Everything else in that row stands: `trace_coverage`, `soak_retries` and every other word equal.

## 1. #809 Part C: decisions that cannot be replayed

### 1.1 The facts

- **`_wait` reads the clock and a live snapshot at every poll and keeps neither** (TG:558-559). The interval row keeps the entry and exit stamps, the release row's time and values, the last poll's slope and the word (TG:636-645).
- **Low coverage is permanent.** One poll under .9 sets `unobserved` (TG:563-564). No later row is then good (TG:574), and the word is `unobserved` (TG:645). So a row that says `released` asserts coverage of at least .9 at every poll. That is the counterexample (GC:49-55).
- **Two other terms depend on the poll time:** the sample's age (TG:574) and, for G0, the status reading's age (TG:584). A failure of either resets a count. The release then comes later or the cap ends the wait. Neither can make a release that the rows do not support.
- **Every other term of a good row is fixed by the rows:** continuity, validity and the two deltas (TG:572-577), the sample slope, the OS level and the pressure state (TG:581-583).
- **The gate is one of the ten** (VR:489-495). The poll loop has no seam outside it: the clock and the reader belong to the runtime process, whose argument list is tested equal to the frozen one (RLD:20136).
- **The final deadline is recorded** (WL:721). The stamp behind a re-arm is not (R1:715-724). Step D's member wall time is measured outside the bundle (R1:1749-1753) and reaches the slot receipt as one scalar (R1:1090).

### 1.2 (a) No trace

**No producer writes a decision trace for Part C, and I authorize neither branch of RL-107.** No file of the ten changes, no wrapper or patch is loaded into the runtime process, and no second slot session is ordered.

- **A trace inside the ten costs a slot session or a survival ruling** (RLD:6059-6063), to make a smoke's evaluator exact. RL-183 1.2 declined that trade for a smaller diff (RLD:20114-20117). The reason has not changed.
- **A trace from outside the ten changes what Part C runs.** It puts I/O in the poll loop of a process W1 will run without it. Part C is the smoke of W1's bytes (RLD:18840).
- **A trace would not be independent.** The process whose decisions are judged would write it. Against later edits the ledger's digests already bind the journal (RLD:20589).
- **1.3 is enough.** It refuses the counterexample and audit 3's first finding, and passes a run with ordinary margins.

**Deferred, not ordered.** If a slot session is ever ordered for a reason of its own, the interval row gains three fields in that commit: each poll's stamp, the newest row's `monotonic_ns` at that poll, and the coverage fraction. Until then RL-183's reading stands: where the unchanged call cannot distinguish two cases, the evaluator takes the failing one (RLD:20127).

### 1.3 (b) The rule

> **A recorded word is accepted only if no admissible poll schedule could have produced a different word from the same rows. A recorded number is accepted if some admissible schedule produces it. Otherwise the verdict is `other_failure` with reason `evidence_unverifiable`. Where every admissible schedule contradicts the record, the reason is the gate's existing decision reason.**

**Admissible instants,** for a row with entry `s` and exit `x`. The two allowances are my choice and are assumptions, not measurements.
- A poll may have happened at any instant in [s, x].
- A sample with finish stamp `f` is *possibly visible* at `u` when f ≤ u, and *surely visible* when f ≤ u − 250 ms.
- A sample is consumed at some instant in [f, min(f + 1.5 s, x)]: one 1 s sleep (TG:599, TG:609), 250 ms of overrun, 250 ms of visibility.

**Why the split.** Coverage, the entry status check, a collector fault, the cap and the deadman change the word. Those are judged over every instant. The two age terms move only the release row, and a release later than it was due leaves the member cooler, not hotter. Requiring them to hold at every instant would refuse healthy runs whose status reading is a second old. They are judged by existence, on the rows the record itself names.

### 1.4 The acceptance test for each witness

`n` is 10 for G0 and 5 for G1 and H (TG:543). `e` is the row whose `monotonic_ns` is the record's `exit_sample_ns`. `D` is the recorded `deadline_ns`.

| # | Witness | `pass` needs | From bound records? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **G0, G1, H: the word `released`** | **(U1)** frozen `_window_coverage` on the surely visible rows is ≥ .9 at every instant of [s, x]. It changes only at row times, finish times, those plus 250 ms, those plus 60 s and grid edges, so it is evaluated at each such point and 1 ns either side. **(U2)** G0 only: TG:532-534 gives the same answer on the surely and on the possibly visible rows at `s`. **(U3)** `f_e` + 1.5 s − s is under the cap. **(U4)** no deadman guarded the wait (R1:1784, R1:1841), or D > x | Yes |
| 2 | **The same row's numbers** | **(N1)** `e` exists, `release` equals its two values (TG:628-630), and f_e ≤ x ≤ f_e + 1.75 s. **(N2)** rows e−n+1 to e exist, and the first is no older than the newest row surely visible at `s`. **(N3)** each passes every row-fixed term of TG:572-583 against the recorded `reference`, which equals the bound one: the window reference for G0, G0's `release` for G1 and H (TG:634). **(N4)** for each, max(f, `pm_observed_ns`) ≤ min(`monotonic_ns` + 2 s, `pm_observed_ns` + 2 s, x); G1 and H drop the status terms. **(N5)** `slope_c_per_min` equals frozen `slow_slope` at some instant of [f_e, x]; `entry_slope_c_per_min` and `entry_sensors` equal the frozen values at `s` on the surely or the possibly visible rows. **(N6)** the stamps equal the gate's begin event (TG:536-538) and `duration_s` is their difference | Yes |
| 3 | **`unobserved`** | The reference was absent at entry; or a stretch of at least 1.25 s exists, before any row that could complete a run, on which even the possibly visible rows give under .9. For G0, x − s ≥ min(300 s, cap) (TG:596) | Yes |
| 4 | **`timeout`** | U1 holds, x − s ≥ the cap, and no `n` consecutive rows of the wait pass N3 and N4 | Yes |
| 5 | **`deadman` in a wait, and every deadman check in the turn and tool loops** (WL:490, WL:516-521, WL:583, WL:595) | Each check lies between two bound stamps a < b of the member. **Passed** is accepted when b < D. **Expired** is accepted when the stop is recorded at or after D and the work before it began before D. A check with a < D ≤ b is unverifiable. Work admitted with a ≥ D is a decision failure | Yes, after the re-arm. A check made before a re-arm is judged against the arm bracket plus the configured seconds, by the same three cases |
| 5b | **The re-arm itself** | D minus the configured `rearm_s` lies between the bound stamps either side of the hook's re-arm, and `deadline_origin` is the name that member's hook writes (R1:1802, R1:1815, R1:1876) | Existence only. The exact stamp has no witness and needs none |
| 6 | **Admission: G0 unreleased, decode budget** (WL:445-452, WL:508) | Exact, from the intervals and the token counts | Yes |
| 6b | **Admission: context limit** (WL:519-528) | An admitted turn: its recorded rendered length plus `max_tokens` is within the limit. If the record carries only a partial count, the check is the partial count, and the report says so. **A rejected turn: `evidence_unverifiable`.** Its length was never recorded and I order no re-render | Admitted: yes. Rejected: no |
| 7 | **Step D `prefill_s`, token cap and `B_D`** | As the builder has them (BR): exact from the turn clocks, the frozen template and R1:1044-1057 | Yes |
| 8 | **Step D's enclosing wall time** | The recorded `member_wall_s` is at least the member's episode span and gives I_D in [0, 1750), the frozen bound (R1:1052). If bound stamps on the same clock bracket `run_member`, it is also at most their difference. Everything derived from it is recomputed exactly from the recorded scalar | Lower bound yes. Upper bound only if a bracket exists; its absence is not a failure |
| 9 | **The native decode-end stamp** | It lies between the turn's last witnessed token stamp and the endpoint's return stamp, with order and counts reconciled as the builder has them (A3:12) | Existence only, and that suffices |

**Why rows 8 and 9 may pass on existence.** Part C is a smoke. Its Step D derives no registered slot, and nothing W1 uses reads either value (RLD:20146). A scalar inside its bracket, with every dependent value recomputed from it, is what a smoke can prove.

**What 1.4 does not prove.** That the poll loop never stalled for more than 250 ms. A stall tends to break N1 or N2 and refuse, not pass. That a release was not due earlier than recorded. That the runtime wrote a true row before its own close (RLD:20779).

### 1.5 Tests owed, and the one check before W1's Part C

1. **The counterexample is refused.** GC's rows with a recorded `released` give `evidence_unverifiable`. Audit 3's 53/60 case stays a decision failure. The passing control moves to rows that hold U1 at every instant; a control at exactly .9 is expected to become unverifiable.
2. **Coverage is monotone in rows** on the suite's fixtures: removing a row never raises the fraction.
3. **One mutation per clause** U1 to U4 and N1 to N6, and per case of rows 3 to 9, each refused with its reason.
4. **No leak.** RL-183c's marker test covers every new check: names and counts leave the process, no value does.
5. **The ten are untouched.** `git diff b2e01464d -- <the ten paths>` is empty; PR #823's comparator at 10 of 10.
6. **Before the one Part C on the final W1 pin,** the replay RL-183 1.3 already orders on the stored records of the counted Part C and F0 run 11 (RLD:20144-20146) runs with 1.4. Output: the verdict word, the failing check names, and per gate the count of rows failing U1 or N4 by term name. No value. Two `pass` words are recorded and the work proceeds. **An `evidence_unverifiable` on a gate check of either run comes to me with those names.** I then choose between widening the two allowances and RL-107's branches. That choice is not made before then.

## 2. The ctl-01 kit

### 2.1 Hidden doses and recovery: wait for the read

**Not frozen today** (RLD:17577). The rule the read is applied through is fixed now, so the read cannot shop for values.
- **Doses stay 128, 256 and 512, two legs each** (RLD:13438), unless `lm-inst-01`'s floor print (RLD:16366-16371) shows the 128 dose under the floor on the GPU rail and on DC-in. Then I raise doses in the freezing line. No dose goes below 128 and no fourth dose is added. A change of dose is kit data and no re-pin.
- **Recovery is sampled inside the member** (CD:33-36), which is RL-169a's requirement (RLD:16703). Its length is five times the return-to-baseline time the read prints, at least 120 s and at most 600 s. The draft's 600 s stands until then.
- **My freezing line** names the three doses, the recovery seconds and the split gap. The kit is issued after it and not before.

### 2.2 Visible caps, turn shapes, split gaps, replay

**Accepted as drafted** (KD `seed_law.scripts`, CD:67-70), on one condition and with one value confirmed at the read.

| Field | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Prefill 2,000; visible 1,024 on hidden and plain legs | Accepted, if 2,000 is a prompt size `lm-inst-01`'s roster reads. If it is not, the kit takes the nearest size that is. Checked at the read |
| Hidden call after G0 and before the visible call | Accepted. The print states that the visible call follows the hidden one |
| Extra turn: 1,024 + 1,024, no gap | Accepted |
| CPU: 512, one-core burn of 10, 30 or 90 s, 512 | Accepted. It is the shape RL-176 B.1's qualifier needs (RLD:18004) |
| Split: 342 + 341 + 341 against plain 1,024 | Accepted |
| Split gap 10 s | Provisional. At the read: 10 s stands if it is at least five times the printed decode-end lag; otherwise the gap becomes five times the lag, rounded up to a whole second |

**The split and plain legs need not replay one token sequence.** Equal total decoded tokens from the same prompt and seed is the requirement, and it is what the runner does (CD:30-31).
- **Why.** Literal replay needs a growing conversation or forced decoding. That is a new measured path on a print-only pair.
- **What the pair then shows, and its limit.** Each split call starts at the same context; the plain call runs about 680 tokens deeper. The print labels the pair "equal counts, same prompt and seed, different context depth", prints each call's start context, and draws no word from the difference.
- **RL-149 §2.5 is amended** (RLD:12542): "the same tokens in one turn and in three with gaps" reads "the same number of decoded tokens, from the same prompt and seed, in one turn and in three with gaps".

### 2.3 One logged envelope, and what the controls print may disclose

**Accepted** (CD:38-47). One envelope per episode whose counts sum the visible calls; hidden work absent from it; `script-work.json` as the ground truth, reached only through its custody hash.

**The print may disclose, per leg:** script kind; the doses (hidden tokens, CPU seconds, gap, recovery); physical call counts and durations; the logged counts; energy above baseline by phase on the GPU rail, the CPU rail, the rail sum and DC-in; joules per hidden token; the dose-response slope with its range; each value in units of `lm-inst-01`'s floor; the 1 % closure check; the qualifier word (RLD:18004).

**It may not disclose:** generated text or token ids; any K or S threshold, score or outcome word; "detected" or any word of that kind; anything from a series member. DC-in is allowed because every ctl leg is conditionless.

### 2.4 Ownership and freeze order

| Thing | Owner | Frozen |
|---|---|---|
| Doses, recovery, gap; the print list and the manifest's cold pass; the disclosure sentence | Research lead | At the read, in one ruling line |
| The kit's issue, pins, ledger, close proof, dates (CT:6) | Lead | After that line and the cold seat of 2.5 |
| Controls print code, output schema, manifest `lm-ctl-01` | Sol builder with an analyst seat (RLD:18125) | Hash committed **before any ctl energy is read** (RLD:17577) |
| The registration's disclosure amendment (RLD:12544-12548) | Lead commits; I supply the sentence | After ctl-01's last span closes and before its look reads. A blind amendment in the deviation log. It does not hold W1's signature |

**Order.** Runner PR admitted, then the read, my line, the cold seat, the issue, the pilot span. The remaining span waits for the pilot's hand-read. The print freeze may come after the legs run (RLD:18014) and must come before the look.

### 2.5 Span layout and seed

- **3 + 9 with master seed `2026111601` is accepted** (KD, CD:73-79). No outcome exists, so a new seed buys nothing. The split and plain legs stay adjacent in one span under one reference.
- **No date rule from me.** ctl-01 prints no per-day error (RLD:18910). `t0_rule: free` stands.

## The ruling: (a)

**Check 1 is a hash test and the tick test.**

1. **The block is frozen by content.** A test reads `joulewise/adapters/mlx_runtime.py` from disk as bytes. It fails unless all three hold:
   - The start line occurs exactly once: `                    # RL-182a: record both boundaries before constructing the events.\n`
   - The end line occurs exactly once: `                text_parts.append(str(getattr(response, "text", "")))\n`
   - The bytes from the first byte of the start line to the byte before the end line have SHA-256 `85ffe1a3cff318c6880d09d72b437c410a18f2dd92395ce62e08956d64c845c5`.

   That is 655 bytes, ten lines, MLX:893-902. It is the same cut CB:52-65 already makes, so the test belongs beside it and the two together pin every byte of the adapter (whole file: `578455fa7b9ffb5582ef6c09ab5428d3078f3b1aea058409d39187de160a9336`).
2. **The tick test stays** as it is (TM:662-711): stamps exactly one tick apart on cache miss, cache hit, uncached and suite item. It is the only part that runs the code, and it catches a change of path outside the block.
3. **The AST helper and its mutant tests go** (TM:567-660 and the two tests after TM:717). Identical bytes imply adjacency and the exact form. The builder deletes them in the same change.

**Why.**
- RL-182a asked for a test that "fails if a later change puts work between the stamps" (RLD:19978). Any later change to these lines now fails. That is the property, stated without a grammar of Python.
- An AST proof has no closed form short of "the statements are these statements". Seven rounds show it. Option (b) written honestly is option (a).
- Every mutant needed someone to edit the source. The guard against a real run going wrong is check 2, on real records.

**What a failing hash means.** The block was edited. The edit comes to me, and the digest changes only in a commit that cites my ruling's id. A runtime pin that moves these lines is the same case.

**Check 2 is unchanged.** Over 10 ms on any W1 turn comes to me before C1 arms (RLD:19979, row 6 at RLD:20011).

**Astra's standard for check 1 is replaced.** A finding on check 1 is now only: an edit inside the block that leaves the hash test green, or a clean adapter that fails the tick test. Mutations outside the block stay out of scope, as the lead set at 07:17.

## 2. The C1 round-2 comparator

**Scope of what I verified.** The paths below are the engine's, under `rl176.`, read from RK and PH at `82542232d`. I did not read the producers of B7 items 1, 4, 5 and 6 or of the RL-149 §4 prints. For those I give the class by leaf type; the adapter owner binds the pointer at the sealed pin. RL-180's tolerances are the interim twin's and govern nothing here.

### 2.1 The classes

Operators are CMP:244-270's. "rel" is |a − b| ≤ bar × max(|a|, |b|). A null agrees only with a null, and the reason beside it is compared exactly.

| Class | Leaf | Unit | Engine wire | Recompute wire | Operator, tolerance | Immutable source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | A ratio of integers: θ, every exact tail and two-sided p, a rate, a share or percentile of counts, a mean or difference of means of counts | none | binary64 | two integers `[num, den]`, lowest terms, den > 0 | **Equal, zero tolerance:** the engine's float equals `num / den` rounded once to nearest | R2 §8 "θ̂ exact rational; p exact rational" (R2:156-158). RK:112-116 shows the engine's floats are single correctly rounded quotients |
| N2 | A trace integral on a powermetrics rail over stamp-defined limits; a sum or mean of such; such a value over an exact count or exact duration; a mean of native samples | J, W, J/token | binary64 | binary64 | rel 1e-9 | BARS `turn_owned_energy_j`, `gross_episode_energy_j`, `predictions_j` |
| N2d | The same on benign DC-in | J, W, J/token | binary64 | binary64 | rel 1e-3 | BARS `dc_benign`; R2:160 |
| N3 | A difference of two joule terms | J | binary64 | binary64 | abs 1e-6 | BARS `residuals_j`, `turn_residuals_j` |
| N4 | A fitted coefficient, slope, standard error or an interval endpoint of one; a product of a coefficient and exact factors | its own | binary64 | binary64 | rel 1e-6 | BARS `fit_coefficients`, `fit_rss`, `u5_values` |
| N5 | A dimensionless continuous statistic | none | binary64 | binary64 | abs 1e-6 | BARS `scores`; R2:160 |
| N5p | The same printed as a percentage | percentage points | binary64 | binary64 | abs 1e-4 | N5 at 1e-6 on the fraction |
| N6 | A duration summed from integer stamps | s | binary64 | integer nanoseconds | Equal, zero tolerance: the float equals `ns / 10^9` rounded once | Same as N1; RK:506, PH:95 |
| N7 | A stamp or reading less a value from a frozen, hashed model; a sensor mean | s, °C | binary64 | binary64 | abs 1e-9 | BARS `u2_values`, `u3_values`, `u4_values` |

- **Why N1 is asymmetric.** RK emits floats only. A float alone cannot show the rational was exact, and the comparator spec's own mutation ("change the rational, keep the float") needs lossless operands on one side. The twin is not yet sealed, so it carries them. The ten frozen sources and #813's wire are untouched.
- **A decision is never taken from a float.** Every word, branch and strict comparison stays an exact compared leaf.
- **A leaf that fits no class refuses** as `unbound_numeric` and comes to me by name. No fallback class exists.
- **Each class is a named family in the bars file,** added before the analysis seal pins that file's digest (R2:191-192).

### 2.3 The leave-task-pair-out metadata AUC

**R2 §6.18's exemption stands and is read narrowly. R2 §11 is satisfied by presence, shape and population, and by nothing about the value.**

- **Why the value is not compared.** The reason is in the registration: `shared_library_print` (R2:122). Both families would call `joulewise.align.metadata_baseline`. Two calls of one function agreeing is not a recomputation, and §11 forbids sharing new outcome arithmetic between families (R2:202). A second implementation of a grouped cross-validated classifier is a new build on a print that carries no word.
- **Why this is not a hidden exemption.** §11 forbids an output hiding in a print-only exemption (R2:201). This one is listed by name, with its reason, at one pointer.
- **Engine side, required.** One leaf at the one path P4:1389 prescribes, inside the time-baseline print. Closed shape: a finite number in [0, 1], or null with a reason from a closed list. Beside it: the held-out pair of each fold, and the members scored in each fold by condition.
- **Compared exactly:** those fold identities and counts, against the independent census (the time baseline's own member population, split by pair). Not against the recompute.
- **Recompute side, required.** At the corresponding path, exactly `{"status": "exempt", "reason": "shared_library_print"}`. A number there refuses. An absent marker refuses. Two absences are never an agreement.
- **Bars.** One family, classification `exempt`, selecting one pointer per side. A selector that matches a second leaf refuses.
- **Mutations owed (R2:205).** Remove the engine leaf: refuse. Change a fold count: hold. Put a number on the recompute side: refuse. Drop or alter the marker: refuse. Change the AUC value: agree, recorded as the one exempt leaf. The value is not a compared leaf, so no detection of it is owed.
- **Integrity of the value** is the analysis seal's: it names `joulewise/align/metadata_baseline.py` by blob, and stage (a) verifies the engine's output bytes.
- **The exception does not spread.** Every other time-baseline row is recomputed and compared under 2.2. No second AUC is asked of anyone.
- **The paper.** Any sentence that quotes this AUC says it was computed by one implementation.

### 2.4 Figures inside claim sentences

E18's sentences leave the figures' format open (RLD:20803-20822). Fixed now, blind.

- **Percentages** (‹x›, ‹y›, ‹c›, interval ends, the context median and range) and the mean difference in turns print to one decimal, rounded half-even from the binary64 value. The words "more", "less", "fewer", "higher" and "lower" come from the test's tail or the estimate's sign before rounding, never from the rounded figure. A value that rounds to zero prints "0.0".
- **Exact p** prints to four decimals, rounded half-even from the rational, or "< 0.0001". The table beside the sentence carries the exact fraction. No comparison with a level is read from the rounded figure.
- **Counts** print as integers.
- **Comparison.** Each side renders from its own leaves. The sentence is an exact compared string, and each substituted figure is one mutation case.

### 2.5 Not mine

The resolver's items 4 and 5 (pins, targets, the paired synthetic outputs, the captured-eligible-no-S fixture) are the integration owner's and the series owner's. RL-185 3.1's two pairs of worlds are the contrast that fixture must reach (RLD:20856-20861).

## 3. The ctl-01 controls print

### 3.1 Closure, the phase boundaries and the whole

**The code is the frozen one: `phase_table` and `qualify_ctl01`, unchanged (PH:71-124, PH:231-252).** RL-176 B.1 asked for "the same code on ctl-01's legs" (RLD:18004).

- **No baseline enters closure.** It is on absolute joules: |Σ phases − whole| ≤ 0.01 × |whole|, the bound included, and every counted segment has a finite half-width and full coverage (PH:115-122). A relative check on baseline-subtracted values would divide by something near zero.
- **The whole** is the trace integral over the episode's own [`start_ns`, `end_ns`] less its gate and hold segments (AT:722, PH:110-112). The print stretches nothing.
- **Rails.** GPU, CPU and package (PH:18). Package is the sum of the adapter's three rails on shared support (PH:45-59); it is the "rail sum" of RL-186 2.3 and of RL-185 §4. The word `qualified` reads these three and not DC-in (PH:238-243). DC-in's closure prints beside them under the same predicate and enters no word.

**The correction. The phase code is given a physical-call view of the leg, not the one logged envelope.**

- **What is wrong today.** The runner returns one logged turn that takes its start and first-token stamps from the first visible call and its counts from all of them (CC:92-96). The frozen tiling calls everything in a turn after its first token "decode" (AT:572-579). On a CPU leg the burn lies between the two visible calls (CC:80-87), so it is inside that one turn, after its first token, and is counted as decode. "Other ungated time" would then hold no burn, and the qualifier's test, that CPU-rail energy of other time rises across 10, 30 and 90 s (PH:239-247), would compare three recoveries.
- **Where the fault lies.** In RL-186. I accepted the single envelope in 2.3 and called the CPU script "the shape RL-176 B.1's qualifier needs" in 2.2 (RLD:21355), and did not check the two against each other.
- **The rule.**

> The controls print builds, for each leg, a view of its episode in which the one logged turn is replaced by one turn per **visible** physical call of `script-work.json`, with that row's start, first-token and end stamps, its delivered tokens as decode tokens and its context tokens as prefill tokens. Nothing else of the episode changes: not its start or end, its gate and hold intervals, its traces or its clock mappings. Hidden calls, the CPU interval, gaps and recovery are not turns. The frozen phase code runs on this view.
>
> Before use the view is checked against the logged envelope: the visible calls' delivered and context tokens sum to the envelope's counts; the first visible call's start and first-token stamps equal the envelope's; the steps are ordered, do not overlap, and lie inside the episode after the G0 gate; the recovery's end is at or before the episode's end. A leg that fails a check prints `not_evaluable` with the check's name and is passed to nothing. It is never repaired.

- **Why this is the same code on the same kind of record.** In a series member each logged turn is one physical call. The view restores that for a leg whose runner summed its calls.
- **What it gives.** Unlogged work lands in "other": the hidden call, the burn, the gaps and the recovery. That is what a reader of the log would see, and it is what the qualifier is meant to test.
- **The envelope stays the logged record.** RL-186 2.3 stands. The print's `calls` and `envelope` rows are unchanged (CS's destinations table).
- **"Other", divided.** The print also splits each leg's other time by the physical record: hidden prefill (hidden start to hidden first token), hidden decode (first token to end), CPU, gap, recovery, and the remainder. The parts tile "other" exactly in nanoseconds or the leg is `not_evaluable`. Their joules use the phase code's integrator on the same trace and mapping. This split is the "energy by phase" of RL-186 2.3 and gates nothing.
- **Each boundary carries RL-176 B.2's 1.0 J timing edge** (PH:20). The print states it.

### 3.2 The baseline for "energy above baseline"

A ctl leg has no hold: its band is `q0`. It has a sampled recovery, with the model resident and the sampler running (CC:88-89).

> A leg's baseline on a channel is the mean power over the last 40 s of its recovery interval, from the recovery's recorded end backwards. A value above baseline is the phase's absolute joules less the baseline times the phase's exact seconds. No second integration is made.

- **Why the recovery's end.** RL-186 2.1 sets the recovery at five times the printed return time (RLD:21343). Its last stretch is the one interval of the leg that the design puts at rest.
- **Why 40 s.** It is one of `lm-inst-01`'s three window lengths, so the baseline's own noise is a printed floor. The shortest recovery, 120 s, holds three such windows.
- **A check that prints and gates nothing:** the mean of the 40 s before that window, less the baseline, in units of the 40 s floor.
- **No baseline.** An incomplete recovery, or a channel with a gap over U1 in the window, gives that leg and channel a null baseline with the reason. Its above-baseline values are null. Its absolute phase table and its closure still print.

### 3.3 Hidden joules per token, the slope and its range

Per hidden leg and channel, all above baseline:

| Quantity | Definition | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Hidden-call energy | The hidden call, start to end | J |
| Its prefill and decode parts | Cut at the hidden call's first-token stamp | J |
| **Joules per delivered hidden token** | The decode part over the tokens delivered. Null with the reason at zero tokens or no first-token stamp | J/token |
| **Dose-response slope** | Least squares with an intercept of hidden-call energy on delivered hidden tokens, over the contributing hidden legs. The intercept prints: it is the unlogged prefill | J/token; J |
| **Its range** | The smallest and largest of the slopes refitted with one contributing leg left out | J/token |

- **Why the slope is on the whole call.** Every hidden call renders the prompt afresh, so its prefill is a cost that does not depend on the dose and belongs in the intercept. On DC-in the pulse's lagged tail falls outside the stamps and the visible call follows at once; that loss is also near constant across doses. The slope is the robust number. DC-in's joules per token are marked "tail cut", as RL-181 2.4 marks the turn energy (RLD:19419).
- **The range is a description.** No interval, no test, no word, and no comparison with the floor is drawn from it.
- **Minimum.** At least four contributing legs covering all three delivered dose levels. Otherwise the slope and range are null, reason `insufficient_legs`, and the per-leg values still print.

### 3.4 Which legs contribute

**Every one of the twelve positions prints a row. No leg is replaced in a print, and a missing input nulls a value and never removes a leg.**

| Case | Per-leg values | Slope and range | Qualifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admitted leg | Print | Hidden legs enter | Passed |
| Short delivery: a call under its cap (CC:70) | Print, labelled `delivery: short`, with requested and delivered counts. Joules per token use the delivered count | **Not in the fit.** Printed beside it as a point | Passed. Closure is about energy, not counts |
| CPU interval incomplete | Print | Not applicable | Passed with no burn dose. The dose set is then incomplete and the word is `no` (PH:244-247) |
| G0 not released; script not dispatched | Row with the disposition, no values | Out | Not passed. Fewer than twelve closing legs is `no` (PH:248-249) |
| `script-work.json` absent or off its custody hash; a view check failed | `not_evaluable`, no physical quantity | Out | Not passed |
| A rail trace or clock mapping missing | That channel null with the frozen reason (PH:76-77); other channels print | Out for that channel | That leg does not close |
| DC-in absent or gapped over U1 | DC-in null for the leg | Out for DC-in | Unaffected |
| Baseline null (3.2) | Above-baseline values null; absolute values print | Out for that channel | Unaffected |
| Instrument floor null for a window | Floor units null with the instrument's reason | Unaffected | Unaffected |

- **Why a short hidden leg is out of the fit.** The kit already calls it unadmitted (`exact_script`). An early stop is a different event from a scripted dose, and one rule, "unadmitted enters no estimate", is simpler than a second one for partial doses.
- **`not_run`** is printed only when no ctl leg was loaded (PH:233-234). Anything loaded and incomplete is `no`, with `all_legs_close` and `cpu_burn_order` beside it.
- **Censored instrument values** change the freezing rules and not the print. They are in 3.7.

### 3.5 The instrument floors and units

**Source.** `lm-inst-01`'s `hold.json`: the SD of window means at 10, 40 and 128 s, per leg and channel (IN:45).

> **Pooled floor.** For channel c and window length w, s(c, w) is the root of the mean of the per-leg variances, weighted by each leg's retained windows less one, over the stage-1 qualified legs whose print is not null. Unit W.
>
> **The floor for a value** integrated over T seconds on channel c is s(c, w\*) × T joules, where w\* is the longest of 10, 40 and 128 s that does not exceed T. Under 10 s, w\* is 10 and the row is marked `under_shortest_window`. One SD; the reader applies a multiple.
>
> **Floor units** are the value over that floor. The print keeps the value in joules, the floor in joules, w\*, T, and the instrument manifest's hash.

- **Why every qualified leg and not the 2,000-token ones.** The hold comes before the turn, so it does not depend on the prompt. Using all legs avoids a selection and gives the most windows.
- **Why the longest window not over T.** If the noise averages down, a shorter window overstates the floor, which is the safe direction. Under 10 s it may understate, hence the mark.
- **The dose-response slope gets no floor units.** It is a rate. Its range is its description.

| Printed thing | Unit |
|---|---|
| Energies, baselines times seconds, floors, closure error | J |
| Power, baseline, pooled SD | W |
| Durations, doses in CPU seconds, gaps, recovery | s, from integer nanoseconds |
| Tokens, calls, context counts | integers |
| Joules per token, slope, range | J/token |
| Floor units, closure's relative error | dimensionless |

**The binding.** The read is restricted, so `lm-ctl-01` reads `hold.json` where it lies, in custody. My freezing line names the sha256 of `hold.json` and of `edges.json` as I read them. A sha256 is a kind the public side may carry (RLD:18862). The `lm-ctl-01` manifest pins both hashes and `lm-inst-01`'s final manifest hash, and stage 2 refuses on a mismatch before any ctl energy is opened.

### 3.6 The CPU rail

`lm-inst-01` reads three channels: GPU rail, rail sum, DC-in (SC:503, the closed `channels` list; IN:30-34). It prints no CPU-rail floor.

**A CPU-rail value prints in joules. Its floor units are null, reason `no_matched_floor`. No other channel's floor is put in its place.**

- **No fourth instrument channel.** It would reopen the v2 schema and RL-181 2.1 for a number that changes no decision. The qualifier's CPU test is an ordering and needs no floor.
- **The burn is still expressed in floor units** where a monitor would meet it: on the rail sum, which contains the CPU rail, and on DC-in.

### 3.7 What waits for the `lm-inst-01` read, and the rules it is applied through

**Fixed now:** everything in 3.1 to 3.6, the print's code, its schema and its hand vectors. The doses, recovery and gap are kit data and the floors are inputs, so the code freezes without them.

**Waits for the read, and nothing else does:**

| Value | Rule, fixed now |
|---|---|
| The three hidden doses | 128, 256, 512 unless 128 is under the floor on both the GPU rail and DC-in (RLD:21342). **"Under the floor" on a channel** means 128 is less than the median, over qualified legs with a value, of the 10 s floor in tokens (`gain.json`, IN:53; RLD:19426). **If raised,** the doses are 2ᵏ × (128, 256, 512) for the smallest k in {1, 2} at which the lowest dose is not under on at least one of the two channels. If k = 2 fails, no kit is issued and it returns to me |
| Recovery seconds | Five times the return time, within [120, 600] (RLD:21343). **The return time** is the largest over qualified legs and the three channels. A value censored as "under" a bound counts as the bound. A leg that never returns in its stream sets 600 |
| Split gap | 10 s if at least five times the decode-end lag, else five times the lag rounded up (RLD:21357). **The lag** is the largest over qualified legs. **If any is "over 1 s",** the gap is the larger of 10 s and the return time above rounded up, and at most 60 s |
| Prefill size | 2,000 if the stage-1 roster holds qualified legs at 2,000; else the nearest size it does hold. The candidate's roster has 256, 2,000 and 19,458 (IN:57) |
| The floor numbers s(c, w) | From the read; hence every floor unit |
| The hashes of `hold.json` and `edges.json` | In my freezing line |

- **Why the largest and not a typical leg.** The cost is bounded: recovery cannot exceed the draft's 600 s and the gap cannot exceed 60 s. A longer rest costs minutes; a short one spoils the baseline of 3.2.
- **RL-186 row 6 is read with this table.** My freezing line quotes the read's figures, the rule and its result, as that row requires.

### 3.8 Hand vectors the tests must reproduce

Written by a seat of another family than the builder's, as RL-181 row 6 has it for qualification.

1. One CPU leg in both forms: on the envelope the burn is in decode; on the view it is in other. This is the regression for 3.1.
2. Closure at exactly 1.00 % passes and just above fails.
3. A hidden leg: baseline, the three energies, joules per token.
4. Six hidden legs: slope, intercept and leave-one-out range, by hand.
5. A short hidden leg: printed, labelled, absent from the fit.
6. An incomplete recovery: null baseline, absolute table and closure still present.
7. w\* at T = 9.9, 10, 39.9, 40, 128 and 500 s; the pooled SD from unequal window counts.
8. A CPU-rail value with `no_matched_floor`.
9. Burns that close but are out of order: `no` with `cpu_burn_order` false.

### 3.9 Not ruled here

The public allowlist, the private file names, the failure status and the disclosure sentence are RL-186 2.4's, at the manifest's cold pass and after the last span (RLD:21372-21381). The implementation base, kit issue and ledger authority are the lead's.

**Blind status.** Blind. No v4 outcome exists, no series member exists and W1 is not signed. No interim, qualification, F2, stability, ctl or transfer energy has been read under any look, and nothing sealed, restricted or measured was opened for this ruling. Section 1 passes a validator and three draft manifests. Section 2 fixes comparison rules for two programs before either has run on data. Section 3 fixes a print's arithmetic before any ctl leg exists, and 3.7 fixes how a read will be applied before the read. No estimator, threshold, level or inclusion rule of the series changes.

**For Ed, plainly.** "Three things, none of which touches the MacBook Pro before Saturday. First, the tool that checks our results-release paperwork passed my final review after eleven audit rounds and can merge; I asked for one small tidy-up later. Second, the program that compares our two independent analyses now has a written tolerance for every number it will see. One number, a baseline classifier score, comes from a shared library, so it is checked for being present and for covering the right episodes, and the paper will say it was computed once. Third, the controls experiment: I found a mistake in my own earlier ruling. The way the runner logs a control run would have filed the deliberate CPU work under 'generating text', so our sanity check would have checked nothing. The fix is in how the analysis reads the record, not in the runner, and costs no machine time."

## 1. The tail's c

**The registered sentence contradicts itself.** `scoring.tail_rule` says "Keep the frozen integration and count clock" and then gives "c = P + (first_stamp + last_stamp) / 2" (`M:363`). `tail_segments` sets `first_stamp` to 3583 and 3071, the closing stamps of the last full blocks (`M:351-360`). So the formula gives P + 3653 and P + 3110.5. The frozen count clock gives P + 3653.5 and P + 3111.

**The frozen clock governs, for three reasons.**
- R-3 defines c as the mean context over the tokens the interval produces, P + (`edge_lo` + 1 + `edge_hi`) / 2 (RLD:15990). The coefficients were fitted on that c.
- The frozen code already scores a long leg's own-prefix tail on the same edges with `tok_first` 3584 (`FI:333`), which is P + 3653.5. A native short leg scored at P + 3653 would differ from a prefix with the same stamps. RL-181 §1.2 requires one scorer for both (RLD:19338).
- The independent oracle derived 3653.5 and 3111 from the brief, without sight of the scorer (`OD:91-92`).

**The mistake is mine in part.** RL-181 §1.2 wrote "c = P + (first + last) / 2" beside the stamps 3,583 and 3,723 (RLD:19338). "First" there meant the first produced token, as in R-3's tail clause. The registration copied it as `first_stamp`.

**The disposition.** The correct formula is:

> n = gaps and c = P + (first_stamp + 1 + last_stamp) / 2.

- **If no qualification receipt exists when the fix reaches main:** re-register. Only that one string in `tail_rule` changes. This is a free pre-receipt re-registration by RL-181 §1.0 (RLD:19303), on the same route as `59557d6e8`. It needs no further ruling. The ledger row takes the new sha256, and every place that quotes the old digest (`SS:9`) is updated.
- **If a receipt exists, or the fix cannot land before the first arm:** the registered bytes stand and no arm waits. The final manifest still equals the registration outside the `PENDING:CODE` slots. The scorer uses the formula above. The lead adds one entry to the public deviation log, quoting the registered sentence, the formula above and this ruling. The look's report cites the entry.

**Why this is allowed after a receipt.** RL-181 §1.0 sends such a change to me (RLD:19303), and this is that referral.
- The tail feeds the L-pair prints only. The word does not use it (RLD:19340).
- The correction is toward a rule dated before any qualification leg existed (RL-166a) and toward the clause the registered sentence itself names.
- No qualification energy has been read. The predicted tails differ by a1 × n / 2, which is 70 × a1 and 39.5 × a1 joules.

**In both cases** the scorer computes c from the segment's two edges, as the frozen code does. `tail_segments` is unchanged. The scorer build does not wait for the re-registration.

## 4. The description looks

Both conventions fill RL-181 §2.4's table (RLD:19423-19425). They are fixed before any F2 or stability energy is read. They answer items 1 and 2 of the executor's resolver (`/Volumes/JW-EXT/scratch/pl-d-desc-looks-executor/resolve-1/FINAL-MESSAGE.md`), which asks the same questions as the suite's FOR-FABLE. Its item 3 is the lead's and is not ruled here.

| Resolver question | Ruling | Value the spec seat binds in `description-edge-ruling.json` |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Rail crossing, for the onset and the decode-end lag: interval start or row-end stamp? | **The start of the first qualifying interval** | Onset lag 0.50 s. Rail decode-end crossings at u = 8.25 and 8.50 s |
| (b) DC-in crossing: interpolated time or first qualifying sample? | **The linearly interpolated threshold time** | Decode-end crossing at u = 8.5078125 s, not 8.55 s. Lags 0.2578125 and 0.0078125 s |
| (c) After the first complete 10 s window fails: every 10 s from sampling start, or every observed sample start? | **Every 10 s from sampling start** | (19, 19, 19) s for GPU rail, rail sum and DC-in on inst-02/L001 |

The same two crossing rules apply to every crossing in both looks: the 10 %, 50 % and 90 % points of the rise as well as the two lags.

### 4.1 The time of a crossing

**Each channel is read as the function its energy is integrated from** (RLD:19413): constant over each rail interval, linear between DC-in samples. The spec seat's recommendation is adopted.

> **Threshold.** θ = hold mean + f × level, with f and the level as RL-181 §2.4 gives them for each print.
>
> **Rail (GPU rail, rail sum).** A rise crosses θ at the **start time** of the first interval in the search span whose mean is at or above θ. A fall crosses at the start time of the first interval whose mean is at or under θ. The row's end stamp is never used as the crossing.
>
> **DC-in.** Let k be the first sample in the search span at or above θ on a rise (at or under θ on a fall), with sample k − 1 also in the span. The crossing is t(k−1) + (θ − p(k−1)) / (p(k) − p(k−1)) × (t(k) − t(k−1)).
>
> **Already across.** If the first interval or sample of the search span already qualifies, the crossing is null with the reason `crossed_before_span`. Every rise or lag that uses it is null.
>
> **Resolution.** Each value still prints its channel's sample period. A lag prints both periods.

- **Why the leading edge.** If interval k is the first whose mean reaches θ on a monotone rise, the true crossing lies between the start of interval k − 1 and the end of interval k. The start of interval k is the middle of that range. The end stamp is its upper limit, so it is late by up to a period on every rail and makes every DC-in lag too small.
- **On the planted trace:** the rails cross at 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 s, DC-in at 0.85, 1.25 and 1.65 s. The onset lag is **0.50 s**. The decode-end fall is at u = 8.5078125 for DC-in, and the lags are 0.2578125 and 0.0078125 s (`HT:54-56`).
- The search spans and the "over 1 s" rule are unchanged.

### 4.2 The recovery search

**Contiguous windows.** The spec seat's recommendation is adopted.

> The anchor a is the latest first observed time among the look's channels on that leg (a rail's first interval start, DC-in's first sample). The windows are [a + 10j, a + 10(j + 1)) for j = 0, 1, 2, … All channels use the same windows. The return time is the start of the first window whose mean is at or under hold mean + 2 × the hold's 10 s SD, less the origin of RL-175 D.4. A window holding a gap over U1 neither passes nor fails; it is skipped and counted. If window 0 passes, the value is "under" a − origin, censored, as before. The search ends with the last complete window before the hold's end. If none passes, the value is "not returned", with the last window's end less the origin as its bound. Each value prints 10 s as its resolution.

- **Why not every sample start.** The threshold uses the hold's SD of contiguous 10 s means (RLD:19417), so the window being compared should be the same kind. Overlapping starts give many tries at one threshold and return early by chance. They also depend on each channel's sample grid.
- **Downstream.** RL-187 §3.7 takes five times the largest return time, within 120 to 600 s (RLD:21800). A value late by up to 10 s lengthens a rest by under a minute. An early one shortens it.
- **On inst-02/L001:** (19, 19, 19) s (`HT:58`).
